lead.description: a shift, from a consistent cause, that falls in the same direction on every repeat

self_checks.title: Balance offset
self_checks.prompt: Readings 21.4, 21.7, 21.2 and 21.5 are taken on a 20 mg standard. What is the estimated systematic error?
self_checks.answer: The mean is 21.45, so the estimated systematic error is 1.45 mg.

self_checks.title: Scatter around the shift
self_checks.prompt: For those four readings, what is the sum of squared deviations from the mean?
self_checks.answer: The sum of squared deviations is 0.13.

self_checks.title: Gauge
self_checks.prompt: A 10 cm gauge is read as 12, 11 and 13. What is the estimated systematic error, and the mean after subtracting it?
self_checks.answer: The estimated systematic error is 2 cm, and subtracting it leaves 10 cm.

overview_sentence: A [systematic error](articles/systematic-error.qmd) is a persistent shift that averaging repeated readings does not remove.
